title: Rerun of P-L4-007 on the figure labels only: still no ordered list shared by the zodiac pages; ZL alone is nominally at p = 0.03 to 0.05, and all of that excess is three labels shared by f73r and f73v at a shift of one place, which RF1b and GC2a do not read the same way
statement: An independent rerun of P-L4-007's check with my own code. Differences from the original, fixed before running: I used only the figure-label loci (unit Lz) of the twelve zodiac pages, 299 labels (15 on f70v1, f71r, f71v, f72r1; 29 on f72r2; 30 on the rest, f70v2 including its one centre label) where the original used 350; glyph strings with word breaks removed; for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1,000 shuffles. Two nulls: labels shuffled over the whole page, and labels shuffled only inside their own ring (the groups the transcription marks). Same position, no offset, ZL3b: 1 agreement in 1,403 comparisons (0.07%). Best offset, exact, ZL3b: 27 against a null mean of 24.9 (p = 0.034 whole-page, 0.050 within-ring). Allowing one glyph of difference: 82 against 76.2 (p = 0.028 and 0.027). Other transliterations, whole-page and within-ring: IT2a exact 19 against 17.8 (p = 0.17, 0.18), one-glyph 82 against 75.2 (p = 0.025, 0.012); RF1b exact 20 against 20.5 (p = 1.0, 1.0), one-glyph 69 against 65.7 (p = 0.15, 0.15); GC2a exact 18 against 18.4 (p = 1.0, 1.0), one-glyph 75 against 72.9 (p = 0.27, 0.23). These are eight tests without correction, and the statistic hardly moves under shuffling (for exact agreement the best offset of most pairs is 1 whenever the two pages share any label, whatever the order), so a p of 1.0 only means the observed total sits at the floor. Power: writing four labels in the same order onto every 30-label page is detected in 20 of 20 trials. Where the ZL excess comes from: only two pairs have two or more exact agreements at one offset. f72r2 and f72v3 share one label twice. f73r and f73v, recto and verso of one leaf, share three labels at the same shift of one place: the 6th, 19th and 24th figure labels of f73r (loci f73r.7, f73r.20, f73r.26) equal the 5th, 18th and 23rd of f73v (loci f73v.6, f73v.19, f73v.25); ZL reads them okeody, okeos, oky on both pages. The first two lie in the outer ring and the third in the inner ring, each one place earlier on f73v than on f73r, and ZL's own clock positions for the three are later on f73r by one and a half to two hours each, so the shift looks like a rotation of the whole wheel, not a counting slip. For that pair alone, shuffling one page gives three or more agreements with p = 0.0045 (0.0009 within rings); multiplied by the 66 pairs examined that is 0.30. IT2a reads the same three. RF1b and GC2a agree on the middle one only: on f73v they read a variant glyph in the first word and a different gallows in the third (RF1b oty against oky), and that leaves them one label common to the two pages. Conclusion: I confirm P-L4-007. There is no list of labels repeating in order from sign to sign. The small nominal excess in ZL is one local coincidence on one leaf that depends on how three or four labels are transliterated, and it does not survive the number of pairs looked at. It is worth one look on the scan, since two of the three words differ between editions.
check: Rerun with the loci stated (unit Lz on the twelve pages, word breaks removed, best cyclic offset per pair, both shuffles). Separately, on the Beinecke scans of f73r and f73v (canvases 1006206 and 1006207), read the labels at loci f73r.7, f73r.20, f73r.26 and f73v.6, f73v.19, f73v.25 without the transliteration in view, and say whether each pair is the same word; if the shift of one place is real it should also show whether the two pages were labelled from starting figures one place apart.
